The Council`s position is that the modification is permitted under Regulation 72(1)(e) of the Public Contract Regulations 2015 (as amended) (non-substantial modifications) and that none of the conditions set out in Regulation 72(8) apply. tender.title: Effect of probiotics on Campylobacter colonisation within the broiler gut
tender.description:
A key component of the FSA work is to reduce the burden of foodborne disease in the UK.  Campylobacter is the leading bacterial cause of foodborne disease in the UK, with chicken meat being the most common food source of exposure to this pathogen.  Campylobacter is widespread in chicken farms, with 60% of UK broilers flocks carrying the pathogen at the point they are slaughtered.  Interventions further down the food chain do not reliably eliminate this pathogen.  Therefore, reducing Campylobacter colonisation on broiler flocks and contamination on chicken meat is a priority area for the FSA as this will contribute towards reducing human exposure and subsequent reported cases of foodborne disease.
A clear evidence gap remains on whether probiotics can consistently affect Campylobacter levels in broilers, across commercial UK farms under routine production conditions, and what magnitude of log reduction is realistically achievable.
To address this evidence gap, the FSA are seeking research proposals for an innovative field-trial based study carried out in real-life intensive broiler houses to assess the effectiveness of a range of probiotics on reducing or delaying Campylobacter colonisation in the gut of broiler flocks.  The research should be designed to answer the following questions:
• “To what extent can commercially available probiotic formulations reduce or delay Campylobacter colonisation in broiler flocks under commercial intensive housed farming conditions, and does this translate into reduced Campylobacter contamination of carcasses at processing?”
• “What is the effect of these formulations on welfare and production performance indicators such as mortality, growth rate, feed conversion efficiency and flock health outcomes?”
We envisage that the proposed study design will consist of several discrete phases.
Given the complexity of controlling Campylobacter in broiler flocks, we would like the inclusion of break clauses at the end of key deliverables to allow sufficient time for the FSA, together with the researcher team, to review the phase findings and determine whether there is sufficient evidence and justification to proceed to the next stage of the project.  If not, then the FSA reserves the right to terminate the project.

tender.description:
North East Lincolnshire Council (The Authority) is undertaking this Preliminary Market Engagement (PME) to test the market's ability to deliver a single, integrated corporate enterprise resource planning (ERP) platform and to inform the options appraisal, procurement strategy and business case.
PME allows local authorities and other contracting authorities in the public sector to engage with a market. PME is designed to encourage the commercial and voluntary sectors to engage with the development process before a procurement is released.
This is the market’s opportunity to express its views, outline market developments and generally influence how solutions to the Authority’s needs might be met. There is nothing for the Authority to evaluate or select in this activity.
PME is not a call for competition. Following PME, the Authority may conclude that procurement is not the best solution to meet a particular strategy outcome. The Authority may conclude that it would be better to do something entirely different to the intent within this PME. It is essential that any organisation participating in the PME understands that a procurement opportunity is not guaranteed.
It is therefore essential that organisations understand that this activity is not part of a procurement exercise and involvement in the PME does not affect an organisation’s positioning either positively or negatively should a procurement opportunity arise subsequently.
The Authority may release a PME to:
• Share information to inform the market of an impending procurement, such that they might make preparations for the tender when it is released; and
• Gather information to develop the Authority’s strategy.
We therefore recommend that if there is no intent to engage in the PME, it is better to sustain interest in activity on YORtender to ensure that any interested party remains informed.

tender.title: Media Handling Tool
tender.description:
This procurement seeks to establish a multi-year contract for the provision of a Media Handling Tool to support Reading Borough Council's (RBC) corporate communications and media management activities. The solution is required to provide a centralised platform through which press releases can be distributed, media enquiries can be recorded and managed, previous public statements can be accessed for reference, and media coverage can be monitored, analysed, and reported upon. The platform also hosts the Council's media website, which enables journalists and media organisations to access press releases, official statements, and associated imagery.   
The service is required to ensure the continued delivery of an effective, professional, and auditable media relations function. It supports timely and consistent communications with the media, maintains a comprehensive record of media engagement and public statements, and provides valuable insight into media coverage and public perception of Council activity. The platform is also a key business continuity tool, particularly during high-profile issues, emergency situations, and periods of increased media interest, where the ability to rapidly distribute information and maintain accurate records is critical.

tender.title: Keel House Weymouth - Consultant Appointment
tender.description:
Keel House, a block of 32 flats in Weymouth owned and managed by Aster Group Limited ("Aster"), suffered a significant fire in the early hours of 20 September 2026. The incident caused extensive damage to the building and has created a complex programme of reinstatement works requiring specialist project management and technical expertise. 
The fire resulted in the complete loss of 16 flats together with a substantial section of the roof, lift infrastructure and associated communal areas. A further eight flats sustained partial damage primarily from smoke, water and toxic fume contamination and require selective strip-out and refurbishment works. The remaining eight flats escaped direct damage and are expected to be reoccupied following restoration of the electrical supply, currently scheduled for 28th October 2026, after which a detailed drying-out programme will commence.
Given the scale, complexity and urgency of the reinstatement programme, Aster requires specialist building consultancy support to coordinate the design, approvals, insurance and delivery process. The project will involve the management and coordination of multiple specialist contractors and stakeholders, including LABC, Planning Authorities, structural engineers, insurance brokers, loss adjusters and insurers.

tender.description:
Future Repairs and Maintenance Services for Manchester City Council's operational estate (including Our Town Hall).
Manchester City Council is undertaking preparatory work for the future procurement of repairs and maintenance services to support the ongoing operation of its estate and of the refurbished Manchester Town Hall.
As the Town Hall returns to full operational use following the completion of refurbishment works, the Council intends to establish a short-term service arrangement to provide essential repairs and maintenance support during the initial occupancy period and whilst longer-term service requirements are reviewed and developed.
In parallel, the Council is developing its future asset management, maintenance and building support requirements with a view to undertaking a comprehensive procurement exercise for a longer-term contract. The future procurement is expected to encompass planned preventative maintenance, reactive repairs, minor capital works and associated technical building maintenance services required to support the safe, efficient and effective operation of Manchester Town Hall as a major civic and heritage asset.
This pipeline notice is being published to provide advance visibility of the Council's future procurement intentions and to support supplier awareness of a potential forthcoming opportunity. The scope, procurement strategy, contract structure, estimated value and anticipated timetable remain under development and may be subject to change.
Publication of this notice does not constitute a call for competition, invitation to tender or commitment by the Council to commence a procurement process or award a contract. Further information will be published in due course should the Council decide to proceed with a formal procurement exercise.
The future procurement is expected to include maintenance activities that reflect the operational, heritage and conservation requirements associated with one of the UK's most significant historic civic buildings.
Estimated contract dates are subject to change at the Council's discretion but it is currently anticipated that the contract length will be 8 years (4+2+2).

The project seeks to secure the long-term future of the facility through replacement of the existing synthetic athletics track surface, associated base repairs and recertification to UK Athletics TrackMark standards.
Accordingly, the Council would like to speak to suppliers with the necessary knowledge, skills and experience of such work about the shape of the imminent procurement through this advertised soft market testing process.
The process will be undertaken strictly as per the Procurement Act 2023 and suppliers who do or not take part in the soft market testing exercise will not be advantaged or disadvantaged and will particularly not confer any advantage to any one supplier.
All respondents to the Preliminary Market Engagement Notice will receive an anonymised summary of the discussions. No bidder confidential information will be shared.

Applying
If you would like to see us to discuss this opportunity, please write in no more than 1000 words describing your interest in the procurement, your past experience in the field and the points you would like to discuss.
Soft market testing is planned to take place between the 7th and 11th December 2026 at the Bannister Outdoor Sports Centre Uxbridge Road, Harrow HA3 6S. Each party will have 3 hours with a common agenda. Please keep these days free as alternative days cannot be offered.
If you are not seen please rest assured this will not disadvantage you in the forthcoming formal procurement. All parties which express an interest will receive feedback from the soft market testing event before the Find a Tender Service notice is published (marking the start of the formal procurement procedure)
Please make your submission via the London Tenders Portal by Thursday 26th November 2026 at Noon.
Project Management
The procurement is being run on a project managed basis, and the Council has put in place resources remains deliverable. Robust governance is in place to ensure that communication channels between the Council and bidders remain robust.
Feedback to potential participants
Feedback will be given to those participating in the forthcoming soft market testing exercise. This will be on an anonymised basis, and we will ensure that information of a commercially confidential nature will not be included in feedback.
Once the formal procurement process begins, GBC will keep participants informed at appropriate stages of the procurement.
Freedom of Information
The Council is subject to the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 1992 and may be obliged, when requested, to disclose information you provide to them even though it may be regarded as confidential. However, the exemption from disclosure applying to information which, if disclosed, would or would be likely to prejudice the commercial interests of any person including the Council (including such information relating to a procurement exercise) will apply, provided that the public interest in maintaining the exemption outweighs the public interest in disclosing the information.
Queries
All questions on this prospectus should be via the London Tenders Portal. Generally, we will respect the confidentiality of questions flagged as such by suppliers. Where we receive queries in relation to this prospectus and we believe the response will be of general interest without violating any confidentiality we will circulate the query and response to all the parties that have expressed an interest.
Canvassing
Participants should note that canvassing or lobbying (defined as communications with the Council or individual stakeholders) outside the channels identified in the Prior Information Notice) might affect their ability to engage with the procurement process. Attention is also drawn to the provisions of the Bribery Act 2010.
Appendix 1 Draft Specification
Main Works
•	Removal and recycling of the existing synthetic track surface.
•	Localised macadam repairs.
•	Potential repair of approximately 800m² of existing macadam.
•	Replacement of approximately 100 linear metres of kerbing where settlement has occurred.
•	Cleaning and refurbishment of drainage channels.
•	Installation of a new World Athletics certified porous polymeric athletics track system.
•	Line marking.
•	Completion testing and certification.
•	Reinstatement and handover documentation.
Delivery Timescales
The Council is targeting delivery during a suitable weather window to allow installation of the new porous surface. The consultancy report advises that porous surface installations are typically undertaken between April and September, subject to weather conditions, and would require approximately 10-12 weeks on site. During this period the athletics track would be unavailable for use.

tender.description: Provision and operation of hired water trailers and related equipment and Demin Water Supply at Hinkley Point B SIte.
tender.procurementMethodRationale:
As part of the UK’s nuclear decommissioning programme, Nuclear Restoration Services (NRS) will begin taking ownership of assets and the responsibility for the Advanced Gas-Cooled Reactor (AGR) sites from EDF Energy Nuclear Generation Limited (EDF) commencing on 1st April 2026 for Hunterston B followed by Hinkley B in October 2026 and marks a key milestone in ensuring the continued safe, secure and cost-effective decommissioning of the UK’s nuclear legacy.
NRS is committed to transparency and collaboration throughout this transfer process, working closely with EDF, regulators and stakeholders to deliver a seamless transfer whilst maintaining the highest standards of regulatory, safety and environmental compliance. In line with this commitment, NRS placed a direct award in accordance with Section 41 of the Procurement Act 2023 and wishes to advise that the EDF contract with Veolia Water Technologies & Solutions, as detailed in this notice, was being novated to Nuclear Restoration Services (NRS) as part of the AGR site transfer process. This is a direct award for the purposes of Procurement Act 2023 and is pursuant to Paragraph 6 of Schedule 5 to the Procurement Act 2023
NRS considered Paragraph 6 applies as the services provided by Veolia Water Technologies & Solutions are critical to the ongoing operation of Hinkley B and it would create significant technical difficulties and unacceptable regulatory risks to NRS for another supplier to supply the services at this time.
Following completion of this novated contract, all future requirements will be progressed through NRS’s established procurement processes and in continued compliance with the Procurement Act 2023 (PA23).
Veolia Water Technologies & Solutions is neither an excluded or excludable supplier.
** Please note **
This is a framework and will be called off as and then required.
